title: Chapter LII

teacherSummary.text: Mrs. Gardiner's letter reveals Darcy found the couple, paid Wickham's debts and settled the marriage, insisting on secrecy. Elizabeth speaks gently but pointedly to Wickham.

writingPrompts.label: Middle School
writingPrompts.text: In “Chapter LII,” how does Austen show the hidden benefactor? Write a paragraph that states your claim, quotes two details from the chapter, and explains how each detail supports your idea. Use the plot you noticed as one piece of evidence.

writingPrompts.label: High School / Common Core
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how Chapter LII develops the idea of the hidden benefactor. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of plot and characterization shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.

writingPrompts.label: AP
writingPrompts.text: Write a literary argument in which you analyze how Jane Austen uses plot in Chapter LII to complicate the reader's understanding of the hidden benefactor. Develop a defensible thesis, select evidence purposefully, and explain how specific choices of diction and syntax create meaning.

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman
writingPrompts.text: Situate Chapter LII within its historical and literary context and argue how the chapter's treatment of the hidden benefactor responds to that context. Engage with at least one secondary perspective (a critic, historian or the author's own statements), integrate quotations smoothly, and cite in MLA style.

writingPrompts.label: Graduate / PhD
writingPrompts.text: Develop an original argument that reads Chapter LII as a hinge in the novel's larger treatment of the hidden benefactor. Position your reading within a named critical conversation (for example formalist, historicist, psychoanalytic, feminist or postcolonial approaches), account for the textual history where relevant, and articulate the stakes of your intervention for scholarship on Pride and Prejudice.

segments.activity: Quick-write and share on the opening question.
segments.script: Good morning, readers. Before we open the book, take three minutes and write your honest answer to this: Why did Darcy want his role kept secret? There is no wrong answer yet; we will test our ideas against the text today.

segments.activity: Model pronouncing, defining and using five key words in context.
segments.script: Today's words include expedite, amounting, compromised, presuming, postponed. Watch how I figure out a word from its sentence before I check the dictionary. Here is the line: “Since such were her feelings, it only remained, he thought, to secure and expedite a marriage, which, in his very first conversation with Wickham, he easily learnt, had never been his design.” My guess comes from the clues around it; the dictionary says: Free of impediment.

segments.activity: Present background, then the significance of the chapter.
segments.script: Let me give you some background that the first readers of Pride and Prejudice would have known. Darcy's act protected the reputation of all the Bennet daughters. Now, why does this chapter matter? Darcy's generosity proves his change and love. As you listen, jot one question you want answered.

segments.activity: Read the anchor passage aloud together; annotate for Plot, Characterization, Theme.
segments.script: Let's read this passage together. I will read the first sentence; you track along. Every time you spot plot, mark it. Turn to a partner: what does the author want us to notice here? I will collect three ideas on the board and we will choose the strongest one together, using the evidence.
